money.note: Individuals gave $118,473; PAC money $360,565; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 12th District since November 2014. Earlier served in the NC House (1994–2014), on the Greensboro City Council (1987–1996) and on her local school board. Taught art for about forty years at Bennett College. Holds a Ph.D. from Ohio State.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed in 2026 by the Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party, Progressive Democrats of America, and Humane World Action Fund (plus several Sway voting groups).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Alma Adams was born or raised, or when she came to North Carolina. We found no documented statements from her on data centers or land development. We also found no documented actions or statements on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, police pay and pensions, gun laws, or school vouchers and charters. Her teacher-pay stance is likewise not documented in the pages available. The Ballotpedia page we had was cut off partway through the 118th Congress key votes, so earlier votes and her state legislative record were not readable. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. No controversies or foreign ties appeared in the pages reviewed, which does not mean none exist.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

money.note: Individuals gave $42,408; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $12,053. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for U.S. House in North Carolina's 12th District in 2026. A finance professional with a finance degree from Santa Clara University (2019). Won the March 2026 Republican primary. No elected office held.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he was raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We could not find his employers or years of work. He has held no office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no statements from him on data centers, limits on out-of-state or institutional home buyers, police pay, school choice or teacher pay. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him, and we found no news coverage of controversies.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says he supports a nationwide ban on property taxes. His campaign site also says property taxes should be abolished.

clean-money.evidence: Pledges 'I will not accept any PAC money.'

workers-first.evidence: Says work visas should be limited and illegal immigration must be addressed. He wants a plan to deport or assimilate illegal immigrants, starting with violent criminals and people abusing government programs, and to cut welfare incentives.

second-amendment.evidence: Supports constitutional carry and says states should not create burdensome legal hurdles to carry a firearm.

pro-life.evidence: Supports a federal abortion ban. He says life begins at conception and that intentionally ending a life should be treated as murder under the law.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says zoning should be limited to genuine infrastructure or pollution concerns, and that if you own property it should truly be yours.
